Class EmailAddressesController

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.emaillink.EmailAddressesController
@RestController public class EmailAddressesController extends Object
POST /who/me/email-addresses asks to add an address, or to change one (replaces), and POST /who/me/email-addresses/confirmations confirms it with the link's token or the code. Both need a browser session for the signed-in identity, signed in within the recent sign-in window: signed out is 401, and an API key or bearer token, even beside the cookie, is 403.

GET /who/me/email-addresses lists the caller's addresses, oldest first, for any signed-in caller. DELETE /who/me/email-addresses/{id} removes one, by the credential id the list shows: it is for a browser session only (an API key or bearer token beside the cookie is 403), needs a recent sign-in, and runs through the LastCredentialGuard, so removing the last sign-in credential is 409. An address that does not exist, one that is not an id at all, and one that belongs to someone else are all 404. Removing the address the session signed in with is allowed and ends that session, which who re-resolves on every request.

  • Constructor Details

    • EmailAddressesController

      public EmailAddressesController(EmailAddressChanges changes, EmailCredentialService credentials, LastCredentialGuard guard, WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository sessions, Executor executor, tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper jsonMapper, Clock clock, Duration recentSignIn)
      Creates the controller.
      Parameters:
      changes - requests and confirms the changes
      credentials - lists and revokes the addresses
      guard - keeps an identity from losing its last sign-in credential
      sessions - reads the browser's who session and its sign-in time
      executor - runs a request's lookup and sending off the request thread
      jsonMapper - reads the request bodies
      clock - the current time
      recentSignIn - how recently the session must have signed in

    • request

      @PostMapping("${who.base-path:/who}/me/email-addresses") @ResponseStatus(ACCEPTED) public void request(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      Asks to add an address, or to replace one, sending a confirmation to the new address. Answered at once with 202, the same whatever becomes of it, so a taken address does not show.
      Parameters:
      request - the request, whose body names the address
